comment: How long a product stays in the Recently Viewed widget, in days.
modal: The retention period, in days, for entries shown by the Recently Viewed Products widget.

comment: How long a product stays in the Recently Compared widget, in days.
modal: The retention period, in days, for entries shown by the Recently Compared Products widget.

comment: Whether recently viewed/compared products are stored server-side rather than only in the browser.
modal: When **Yes**, the recently viewed/compared lists are synchronised to backend storage, so they follow a signed-in customer across devices instead of living only in the browser.

comment: The default layout of product lists — grid, list, or a toggle between them.
modal: How category product lists are displayed by default: **Grid Only**, **List Only**, **Grid (default) / List**, or **List (default) / Grid** (the latter two let shoppers switch).

comment: Whether the storefront reads categories from flat (denormalized) tables.
modal: When **Yes**, category data is served from a flat table for faster reads. A legacy performance option; leave off unless a specific setup requires it.

comment: Whether the storefront reads products from flat (denormalized) tables.
modal: When **Yes**, product data is served from a flat table for faster reads. A legacy performance option; leave off unless a specific setup requires it.

comment: The fallback images shown for products that have no image of their own.
modal: Upload the placeholder images (base, small and thumbnail) used wherever a product is missing its own image.

comment: Whether accented/non-Latin characters are transliterated when building product URL keys.
modal: When **Yes**, characters like 'é' are converted to ASCII when a product's URL key is generated, producing cleaner URLs.

comment: The character placed between parts of the page title.
modal: The separator (e.g. `-` or `|`) used to join segments of the HTML page title.

comment: Whether a canonical link meta tag is added to category pages.
modal: When **Yes**, category pages emit a `rel="canonical"` tag pointing at the preferred URL, helping search engines avoid duplicate-content issues.

comment: Whether a canonical link meta tag is added to product pages.
modal: When **Yes**, product pages emit a `rel="canonical"` tag pointing at the preferred URL (useful when a product is reachable under multiple category paths).

comment: Whether the category filter is shown in layered navigation.
modal: When **Yes**, layered navigation includes a category filter alongside attribute filters.

comment: How many category levels deep the top navigation menu renders.
modal: The maximum category depth shown in the storefront top menu. A smaller value keeps the menu shallow on deep category trees.

comment: Whether date-type custom options use a JavaScript date picker.
modal: When **Yes**, date and time custom options are entered through a JavaScript calendar instead of separate dropdowns.

comment: The order in which the day, month and year inputs appear for date custom options.
modal: Sets the arrangement of the day, month and year fields for date-type custom options, to match local date conventions.

comment: Whether time custom options use a 12-hour or 24-hour clock.
modal: Chooses between a **12h (AM/PM)** and a **24h** time format for time-type custom options.

comment: Enables the RSS feed of new products.
modal: When enabled, a public RSS feed of newly added products is published. (RSS feeds must also be enabled globally.)

comment: Enables the RSS feed of special-price (sale) products.
modal: When enabled, a public RSS feed of products on special price is published.

comment: Enables a per-category product RSS feed.
modal: When enabled, shoppers can subscribe to an RSS feed of products within a top-level category.

comment: The default page layout for product pages.
modal: The layout (e.g. 1 column, 2 columns left/right, 3 columns) applied to product pages that don't specify their own.

comment: The default page layout for category pages.
modal: The layout applied to category pages that don't specify their own.
